data.why: The repository ships ready-to-upload sample/demo/synthetic patient CSVs and lab-format per-modality files for the Lab Data Converter tab, so no synthetic data needs to be authored.

goals: upload a patient's multi-omics profile (mRNA/miRNA/methylation/CNV) and get a predicted cancer molecular subtype with a confidence score
compare predictions and feature attributions across XGBoost, IntermediateFusion, and PathwayAwareFusion models for the same patient
inspect SHAP (tree models) or Integrated Gradients (fusion models) feature attributions, broken down by omics modality, to see which genes/features drove a prediction
review KEGG pathway-level attention weights for the PathwayAwareFusion model to connect predictions to known cancer biology
convert raw hospital-format per-modality lab CSVs (log2, raw counts, beta values, or z-scored) into a prediction-ready row via the Lab Data Converter tab
review aggregate model comparison metrics (F1, AUC, calibration, ROC curves, confusion matrices, ablations) across both cancer cohorts

review.summary: The tree describes what this demo is for: classifying TCGA multi-omics profiles with three pretrained models, explaining each call, benchmarking the models, and converting raw lab files. All 14 screens I opened support their nodes. Before filing, it needs these fixes: one misleading general label (the pathway attention is cohort-level, not per-prediction), the converter phase marked as conditional, the f3/f4 overlap removed, and two missing features added (latent-space viewer and calibration panel).
